articles.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第3週：日曜日の試合の要点、疑問点、ファンタジーの視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの取材記者がすべての試合に反応し、日曜日の各試合から浮き彫りになった最大の疑問に答えます。第3週から分かったことは以下の通りです。
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, while the Browns won their second straight game.

The late window was filled with close games, with all four contests separated by a touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter. The Ravens-Cowboys matchup was the most exciting of the bunch in Rio de Janeiro, ending on a time-expiring, winning field goal by Baltimore's Tyler Loop.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

DAL-BAL | LV-NO

MIN-TB | ARI-SF

SEA-WSH | CAR-CLE | CIN-PIT

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

Catch up on Thursday's game:

ATL-GB

Baltimore 34, Dallas 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Ravens

Did the Ravens exorcise their penchant for fourth-quarter collapses? Lamar Jackson and the Ravens gave an authoritative response to the "same old Ravens" narrative. Tyler Loop's 56-yard field goal with no time remaining lifted Baltimore to an improbable comeback. With seven seconds remaining, Jackson completed a 26-yard pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers, who was a game-time decision because of a hamstring injury. It was redemption for Loop, whose errant 44-yard field goal attempt ended Baltimore's playoff hopes last season. Over the past six seasons, the Ravens have lost an NFL-worst 15 games when leading through three quarters. But they found a way to win Sunday.

Stat to know: With two touchdowns, running back Derrick Henry became the oldest player (32 years, 166 days) in NFL history to score six touchdowns in the first three games of a season. His 34 career games with multiple rushing touchdowns are the most among active players -- 16 more than the next-closest players (Josh Jacobs and Jonathan Taylor with 18). -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Cowboys

Is this any different than the Cowboys' past two seasons? The Cowboys showed moxie to come back from an 11-point deficit, but ultimately, couldn't hold on. Why? A defense that was worn down and worn out. With 7:29 left, the offense had a chance to run down the clock but held the ball for only 1:44. Similar to 2024 and 2025, the Cowboys are 1-2 after two games. The comeback showed some fight, but now they won't get back to work until Tuesday due to traveling back from Brazil. articles.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
articles.description: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. On the flip side, fantasy stars Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jonathan Taylor and Chase Brown had disappointing games.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the third week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 3

1. Jahmyr Gibbs, RB, Detroit Lions

He's sure proving worthy of that No. 1 overall pick. He has scored at least 23 fantasy points in all three games, posted 75% snap and 78% rushing shares, and he has totaled an easily position-best 98.3 points for the season. That latter number ranks 15th in history through three team games of any season. Isiah Pacheco's back and MCL injuries have locked Gibbs in as a three-down dynamo, and the odds are good that he will maintain his positional lead in fantasy points for the duration of 2026. -- Cockcroft

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, and Sam Darnold, QB, Seattle Seahawks

It's incredible to think that Smith-Njigba is off to the stellar start that he is despite Darnold having missed nearly all of the first two weeks due to injury and the team's running game having been only so-so thus far. Smith-Njigba scored 35.36 fantasy points, giving him 104.06 through three games, the fourth most ever through that many by any player. Meanwhile, Darnold threw a pair of interceptions in his return to the lineup, but he didn't seem at all slowed by the glute injury, finishing with 27.66 points of his own. Smith-Njigba's elite play should bring Darnold's fantasy utility up, and the two have a good matchup against the struggling Los Angeles Chargers in Week 4 before hitting a tougher stretch of the 2026 schedule (SF, @DEN, KC in Weeks 5-7). -- Cockcroft

3. Joe Burrow, QB, and Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

In the Week 3 loss to the Steelers, Burrow notched his best numbers of the season, completing 75.7% of his throws for 282 yards and three touchdowns, plus he rushed for 13 yards (22.58 points). Chase caught nine of a team-high 12 targets for 98 yards and a score (24.8 points). That gives Chase two straight games of 24 or more points after that rough opening week. Chase will remain a top-three play at wide receiver for Week 4, while Burrow -- who has thrown for at least two touchdowns in back-to-back games -- will be a lower-tier QB1 in my ranks. -- Bowen

4. Geno Smith, QB, Garrett Wilson, WR, and Kenyon Sadiq, TE, New York Jets

In a positive matchup versus the Detroit secondary, Smith scored a season-best 26.04 points, throwing for 321 yards and four touchdowns. Wilson caught 10 of a team-high 13 targets, finishing with 107 yards and a touchdown (26.7 points), plus Sadiq posted his first breakout game, bringing in seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score (23.5 points). articles.headline: Ravens' jab at Cowboys after win in Rio leads Week 3 trolls
articles.description: The Baltimore Ravens followed up their last second victory over the Dallas Cowboys with a petty post.
articles.body:
The long travel for an international game can make a victory even sweeter. In the Baltimore Ravens' case, it made the postgame troll just that much better.

The Ravens defeated the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 in Rio de Janeiro following a last second go-ahead field goal by Tyler Loop. It marked the NFL's first game in Rio and it surely lived up to the hype.

With the score tied at 31, Baltimore received the ball with seven seconds remaining. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson connected with wide receiver Zay Flowers for 27 yards to set up a 56-yard boot from Loop. The kicker nailed it, giving Baltimore the win and a happy flight back home.

Last Wednesday, Jackson was asked if he expected the Cowboys to have a large contingent of fans in Rio since they are known as "America's Team." The quarterback said "this is America, that's Brazil, so we'll see." The Ravens remembered the moment. They shared a video of running back Derrick Henry dashing past defenders toward his throne, while quipping that Baltimore is "Rio's team now." Flowers also said postgame: "We are Brazil's team."

Here are other top trolls from Week 3.

Pittsburgh Steelers 30, Cincinnati Bengals 27

An early-season AFC North clash predictably went down to the wire.

Facing a three-point deficit with 2:15 left in the game, the Bengals received possession and started driving. They reached the Steelers' 38-yard line, but Pittsburgh defensive tackle Derrick Harmon sacked quarterback Joe Burrow, resulting in a fumble the Steelers recovered to win.

Ever the trollers, the Steelers wouldn't pass up on the opportunity to poke fun at their division rivals with cats being the theme. The Steelers posted a victory image with the caption: "meoW," a video of a cat doing a viral dance and another cat photo captioned: "raWr."

Washington Commanders 33, Seattle Seahawks 31

Washington defeated the Seahawks on Sunday, snapping Seattle's 13-game win streak. The Commanders entered the game with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center due to Jayden Daniels' elbow injury.

Mariota delivered by throwing for 183 yards and three touchdowns. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold started for the first time since an oblique injury forced him out in Week 1. Darnold had 379 passing yards and four touchdowns but two interceptions -- the latter of which resulted in a pick-six with 3:57 left in the game.

The Commanders went straight to trolling after the win. They shared a video from the hit comedy show "The Office" where Jim delivers coffee to Dwight, who can pick it up only with his toes and ends up spilling the hot drink on himself. In this case, Jim is the Commanders, delivering an "L" to Dwight, the Seahawks.

Buffalo Bills 24, Los Angeles Chargers 16

Buffalo stormed back to defeat Los Angeles and remain undefeated.

articles.description: Sunday of Week 3 has seen 13 games played, with Lamar Jackson, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam Darnold having big stat days.
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season continued Sunday with 14 games, including nine in the early window, and we'll have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In the early window, Jaylen Warren had a career outing in the Pittsburgh Steelers' win against AFC North rival Cincinnati Bengals, Jameis Winston stepped in to lead the New York Giants to a victory over the Tennessee Titans and the Washington Commanders slipped by the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Among the highlights from the afternoon slate of four games, the Baltimore Ravens stunned the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro on a Tyler Loop 56-yard field goal and the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after beating the Saints in New Orleans.

The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams in primetime to cap off the day, so keep checking here for "Sunday Night Football" highlights.

articles.headline: Kirk Cousins passes for 3 TDs and the unbeaten Raiders come back to top the Saints 35-27
articles.description: — Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns, and the Las Vegas Raiders overcame an 11-point second-half deficit to beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday and remain unbeaten under rookie coach Klint Kubiak.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Kirk Cousins passed for 248 yards and three touchdowns, and the Las Vegas Raiders overcame an 11-point second-half deficit to beat the New Orleans Saints 35-27 on Sunday and remain unbeaten under rookie coach Klint Kubiak.


              The game shifted on a play that will be seen as controversial and unjust by some — and certainly Saints fans.


              The series that led to the Raiders' go-ahead score began when Las Vegas defensive end Malcolm Koonce sacked Tyler Shough as the Saints QB started his throwing motion.


              The ball went backward and was ruled a fumble that was recovered by the Raiders — a different ruling than was made after a similar play involving the Saints in Week 1 at Detroit. On that play, an apparent New Orleans strip-sack of the Lions' Jared Goff was ruled incomplete on video review after the Saints thought they had recovered a fumble for a touchdown.


              The Superdome crowd booed as officials, following a video review, upheld the call that the play had resulted in a turnover on the New Orleans 45.


              Six plays later, Cousins connected with Cody White for a 4-yard touchdown to make it 28-27.


              Cousins gave Las Vegas (3-0) an eight-point lead with a 4-yard TD pass to Brock Bowers. The Saints (1-2) got the ball twice more with a chance to tie it, but one drive stalled on fourth down and another on Juwan Johnson's fumble with 1:02 left.


              Shough passed for 255 yards and a career-high four touchdowns — including two to Johnson. Shough's other scoring passes went to Noah Fant from short range. But the second-year QB also turned the ball over twice, first on his fumble and later on an interception that set up the Raiders' final scoring drive.


              Bowers, making his season debut after coming back from a knee injury during training camp, caught 10 passes for 116 yards and his short TD. Mike Washington ignited the Raiders' comeback with a tackle-breaking 36-yard scoring run that cut New Orleans' lead to 27-22 in the third quarter. Matt Gay kicked three field goals for Las Vegas, which also failed on a pair of 2-point conversions after second-half TDs.


              New Orleans' Chris Olave caught nine passes for 107 yards, his second 100-yard game this season.


              Injuries
              Raiders: WR Jack Bech left the game with a forearm injury.


              Saints: LB Pete Warner left in the first half with a neck and shoulder injury (stinger). ... RB Travis Etienne left with an apparent hamstring pull. Edge rusher Anfernee Jennings left with a knee injury.


              Up next
              Raiders: Host Kansas City next Sunday.


              Saints: Host Atlanta on Monday, Oct. 5.


              ----


              
                See AP’s full NFL coverage here

articles.headline: Sam Darnold laments 'bad decision' in return for Seahawks
articles.description: Sam Darnold's return from the glute injury that sidelined him for most of the Seahawks' first two games was shaping up to be memorable until a "bad decision" late proved costly against the Commanders.
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- Sam Darnold's return from the glute injury that sidelined him for most of the Seattle Seahawks' first two games was shaping up to be memorable.

His third touchdown pass against the Washington Commanders on Sunday tied the game at 24 in the fourth quarter, capping Seattle's rally from a 14-point deficit and putting the defending Super Bowl champion in position to extend its franchise-record winning streak to 13 games.

Then Darnold made what he called "a bad decision" -- a throw over the middle that was intercepted and returned for a touchdown. His second pick of the day and Seattle's third turnover against Washington was too much to overcome in a 33-31 loss at Northwest Stadium.

"Obviously, I can't turn the ball over the way that I did," said Darnold, who threw for a career-high 379 yards. "We can't turn the ball over as an offense and be inefficient and expect to win games. But ... you've got to tip your cap to the Commanders. They played a really good game. We're just going to continue to look at the film, look at it tomorrow and I think it really starts with looking in the mirror and seeing how everyone can be better and improve."

Darnold threw another touchdown pass in the closing minutes, but the Seahawks couldn't get the stop they needed to get the ball back to their offense, and so ended the NFL's longest winning streak since the Kansas City Chiefs won 15 straight over the 2023 and '24 seasons.

With the Commanders missing quarterback Jayden Daniels and several other starters, the Seahawks closed as 8.5-point road favorites. This marked their largest upset loss in terms of point spread since the New York Giants beat Seattle in 2020 as 10.5-point underdogs, according to ESPN Research.

Turnovers and the absence of a run game were the story for the Seahawks (2-1) as they lost on the road for only the third time since Mike Macdonald became their coach in 2024.

Rookie running back Jadarian Price lost his second fumble in as many weeks in the first quarter, leading to the Commanders' first touchdown. Darnold was intercepted in the third quarter when his throw to Jaxon Smith-Njigba was deflected at the line of scrimmage and caught by linebacker Sonny Styles. That led to another Washington touchdown.

On the pick-six, Darnold was trying to hit tight end AJ Barner on a short, play-action throw over the middle, but backup linebacker Kain Medrano jumped in front of it and returned the interception 50 yards to the end zone.

"Just a bad decision," Darnold said. "The end did a good job of not letting me escape to the outside and I had to make a quick decision, and I should have dirted it at his feet ... I saw him. He made a really good play, but that's a ball I've got to throw away."

Two of Darnold's four touchdown passes were to Smith-Njigba, who now has six receiving scores in three games. Per ESPN Research, Smith-Njigba is the first player since Calvin Johnson in 2011 with six receiving touchdowns through the first three games

articles.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
articles.description: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「自分には関係ない」元マンC監督のマンチーニ氏、有罪報道を一蹴
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・マンチーニ氏は、自身が指揮を執っていた期間に犯したとされる財務違反について、古巣のマンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグから有罪と認定されたとする報道を一蹴しました。
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm. 

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
